gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 30?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts from the Met Office and supporting models indicate a daily maximum of 22°C in London on August 31, 2026, under breezy conditions with early cloud breaking to sunny spells and scattered light showers around midday that fade westward.** 

These conditions, driven by Atlantic low-pressure influences and moderate westerly winds, limit daytime heating while preventing significant overnight radiative cooling. Historical late-August baselines for London average highs near 20–21°C, so current guidance sits slightly above normal but constrained by cloud cover and precipitation timing. 

Model runs show broad agreement on peak values in the 21–23°C range, with limited potential for brief clearing to push toward 24°C or persistent showers holding it at 21°C. Market-implied probabilities (22°C at 48.5%, 23°C at 34%) closely track this consensus, reflecting trader assessment of official guidance and typical model spread for the resolution criteria of the recorded daily high. No sharp forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24–48 hours.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and private model runs show New York City highs on September 1 clustering in the low-to-mid 80s °F, with the tight 25.5% market split between 84–85 °F and 86–87 °F reflecting uncertainty over afternoon convective timing and cloud cover. Southwest flow, high boundary-layer moisture, and a 60–70% chance of showers or thunderstorms will limit insolation and potentially cap peak temperatures, while clearer intervals or delayed development could allow readings near 87 °F. These values sit slightly above the 1991–2020 climatological average of 80.7 °F but well below historical extremes. Updated model guidance and observed trends on the morning of September 1 will drive final resolution within the narrow temperature bins.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources including WeatherBug, Globalmeteo, Yr.no, and others indicate a high of approximately 23–24°C (73–75°F) for Munich on September 1, 2026, under partly cloudy skies with light westerly to northwesterly winds and minimal precipitation risk.** This aligns closely with the historical average high of 22.2°C for the date and places the market-implied probabilities—led by 24°C at 53.5%—in line with the expected range.

Primary drivers include a stable high-pressure pattern limiting strong warm-air advection or clear-sky radiative heating that could push readings to 25°C or higher, while light winds and moderate humidity prevent rapid cooling below 23°C. Ensemble model consensus shows low spread, with most runs clustering in the 23–24°C band and only modest upside risk if afternoon clearing intensifies.

Recent data reinforce this positioning: no significant forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24–48 hours, and early-September climatology supports near-normal to slightly above-normal values without notable heat-wave signals. Traders therefore assign the bulk of probability mass to the narrow 23–25°C window, reflecting both the tight scientific guidance and the inherent uncertainty in local boundary-layer processes that can produce 1–2°C variations.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts for Tokyo's high temperature on September 1, 2026, center on 29–31°C, aligning closely with the market's leading outcomes (30°C at 33.5%, 29°C at 31.0%).** 

Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency projects a high of 30°C under mostly cloudy skies, with light easterly winds and only low precipitation chances. International models and private services show a tight cluster around 29–31°C, reflecting typical early-September conditions as summer transitions toward autumn. Historical normals for the date sit near 30°C, providing a stable baseline absent strong anomalies.

Differentiating factors among these close outcomes include daytime cloud cover and boundary-layer moisture. Persistent stratiform clouds and dew points near 21–23°C limit surface heating, favoring the lower end (29°C) if insolation stays reduced. Any breaks in cloudiness or slightly drier air could push readings to 30–31°C, especially with light winds allowing modest warming. Model runs show minimal disagreement on steering patterns or intensification, keeping probabilities balanced. No major typhoon or frontal passages are expected to alter the setup before resolution. 

Upcoming JMA updates and refined model outputs on the final 24 hours will likely be the key drivers for any late shifts in trader positioning.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official National Weather Service forecasts for August 31, 2026, center the daily high near 79–80°F at Central Park and LaGuardia Airport stations, with Kennedy Airport slightly cooler at ~79°F.** This consensus directly supports the market’s leading 78–79°F bin (51% implied probability), reflecting trader alignment with NWS model runs that incorporate persistent cloud cover, light northeast-to-southeast winds, and only modest afternoon heating under partly to mostly cloudy skies.

Cloud cover and a modest chance of showers (20–30% during peak heating hours) limit insolation and cap temperature rise, while high dew points near 70°F add humidity without extreme heat-index amplification. Recent days show a cooling trend from mid-August peaks above 90°F, consistent with seasonal transition and an approaching warm front that keeps daytime maxima in the upper 70s to low 80s. Ensemble guidance shows limited spread around these values, with the slight edge toward 78–79°F over 80–81°F (15%) arising from verification tendencies for urban stations and the timing of any sea-breeze or cloud effects.

Traders have priced in this data-driven outlook, where 76–77°F (27%) remains plausible if clouds thicken further, but higher bins (>82°F) carry low probability given the stable pattern and official guidance. Updated model runs or afternoon observations could shift odds if skies clear more than expected.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Cloud cover, light northeast-to-southeast flow, and increasing humidity are capping daytime heating across New York City on August 31, 2026, keeping the highest temperature most likely in the 76–79 °F range.** Official National Weather Service forecasts for Central Park and surrounding airports project a mostly cloudy day with highs near 79–80 °F, while several private models and real-time observations trend a few degrees cooler. Light onshore winds off the Atlantic and widespread stratus have limited solar insolation, consistent with the recent pattern of below-normal maxima (recent days in the mid-to-upper 70s). 

This setup explains the market’s strong consensus on 78–79 °F (46.5 %) and 76–77 °F (33.5 %), with only modest probability assigned to 80–81 °F. Historical August 31 normals near 81 °F are unlikely to be reached under the current synoptic regime, and afternoon showers or thunderstorms will further suppress the peak. Traders are therefore pricing the outcome primarily on the latest NWS guidance and observed trends rather than climatology.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Met Office position 22°C as the most likely maximum temperature for London on September 1, 2026, with supporting guidance indicating a range of 21–23°C under partly cloudy skies and light winds.** High pressure is building across southern England, promoting mostly dry conditions with sunny intervals that support daytime warming close to the early-September climatological average of roughly 20–22°C. Ensemble guidance and regional outlooks show limited spread, with minimal risk of significant rain or stronger winds that could suppress temperatures.

The market's heavy weighting toward 22°C (50.5%) and 23°C (39%) reflects this narrow forecast envelope, where small differences in cloud cover or timing of any isolated showers could shift the daily peak by 1°C. Longer-range signals of possible warm spells later in September have not yet altered the immediate synoptic setup for the first of the month. Updated model runs or Met Office briefings tomorrow morning represent the key near-term data points that could refine these implied probabilities before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent short-range forecasts for Tokyo on September 2, 2026, cluster around daily highs of 30–33 °C, with the strongest model consensus favoring 31–32 °C.** This distribution explains why those two outcomes command the highest market-implied probabilities (39.5 % and 28.5 %). Multiple operational models and guidance from sources such as WeatherBug, Met Office, and local ensembles show partly cloudy to mostly sunny conditions, light southerly winds, and minimal precipitation risk, allowing daytime heating to reach the low-to-mid 30s °C before any frontal influence arrives later in the week.

**Forecast models and recent observations position 29°C and 30°C as the leading outcomes for Tokyo’s September 1 high temperature, with market-implied probabilities of 42.5% and 32.0%.**

Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and multiple numerical weather prediction runs converge on a daytime maximum near 29–30°C under mostly cloudy skies, light northeasterly flow, and moderate humidity levels that limit strong surface heating. Recent late-August observations show daily highs stabilizing around 28–29°C amid persistent cloud cover and weak winds, consistent with the early-September climatological transition from peak summer warmth. 

These conditions reduce the likelihood of significant further warming or rapid cooling, keeping the distribution tightly centered on 28–30°C while assigning only modest probability to outliers. Traders are weighting the consensus of short-range model guidance and the absence of disruptive synoptic features—such as stronger onshore flow or clearing skies—that could shift the outcome outside this narrow band.
